summary: iterquarry acts as a loader stub that decrypts and executes an opaque sealed module from an unpinned 'libseal' dependency
details: iterquarry 2.1.2 presents itself as an iterator utility library but is structured as a thin facade over a sibling PyPI package 'libseal'. pyproject.toml declares dependencies = ["libseal"] with no version constraint, so whatever version resolves on PyPI at install time is pulled in and its top-level code runs when iterquarry is imported (recipes.py runs 'from libseal import PACKAGE_ROOT, LibsealError, load_sealed_sync, read_module, seal_sync' at module scope, reachable from the package __init__). The advertised pairwise() API in recipes.py then calls load_sealed_sync(file=SEALED, module_path="quarry", password="pairwise") to decrypt a sealed module shipped inside libseal's install directory using a hardcoded password, and immediately invokes quarry.buffer() in-process. The actual executed code is opaque encrypted content delivered by an unpinned external dependency, with no integrity check, and the decryption password is embedded in the loader. The package's own code contains no legitimate iterator functionality that would require this execution pattern; its sole observable effect is to hand control to arbitrary code packaged inside libseal.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
